paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Devarim 10 — “And this is what they said (Nedarim 22b): ‘Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah… and the book of Yehoshua,’ which is the Oral Torah that Moshe received from Sinai and handed to Yehoshua.” Connection: Both expound this Gemara on the Oral Torah contained within the Written Torah and handed down through Yehoshua.

paragraphs.text: Makkos 11a — "Why was the passage of the cities of refuge said in harsh language, as it is written, 'And Hashem spoke (vaydaber) to Yehoshua, saying: Speak to the Children of Israel, saying: Assign for yourselves the cities of refuge' (Yehoshua 20:1–2)? paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 49b — “Ten measures of wisdom descended to the world: the Land of Israel took nine, and the whole world took one. Ten measures of beauty descended to the world: Jerusalem took nine, and the whole world took one.” The first statement grounds Rav Tzadok's association of the Land with Torah wisdom. The measure is the Gemara's figurative language, not a numerical survey.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 29b (Tzav) — "So Torah scholars, the children of the King and the Queen, are called Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim. paragraphs.text: Zohar I, Mikeitz 202a — “We learned: A person should always rouse the good inclination against the evil inclination and strive against it. If it departs from him, well; if not, he should occupy himself with Torah, for there is nothing that breaks the evil inclination except Torah. If it departs, good; if not, let him remind it of the day of death in order to break it.” The Zohar gives a sequence of active resistance, Torah and remembrance of death. Rav Tzadok emphasizes the Oral Torah's lived study as the means of transforming the inward enemy.
